instruction: Look at `board.brd` in EAGLE. The board has one 8-pin IC (IC1) placed at coordinate (30, 15) mm with rotation R0, plus three 100 nF decoupling capacitors (C3, C4, C5) that are currently in dead space far from the IC. All three caps are already netted to the VCC signal (which terminates at IC1's pad 8). Your job: use the MOVE command in the board editor to drag C3, C4, and C5 so that each cap's origin (its <element x, y> coordinate) sits within 2 mm of IC1's VCC pad (pad 8), which lies at global coordinate (26.19, 18.81) mm. You may keep or change each cap's rotation - only the origin coordinate is checked. Save the updated board as `/home/user/Desktop/answer.brd`. Requirements: 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.brd` parses as XML. 2. Elements IC1, C3, C4, C5 are all still present (no deletions). 3. The VCC signal still lists contactrefs for IC1/8 and each of C3/2, C4/2, C5/2. 4. Each of C3, C4, C5 has an origin within 2 mm of (26.19, 18.81).

command: import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(15); pyautogui.hotkey('shift', 'tab'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter')
